messages:
Alex: Heads-up on FinBank POC. They're asking for a private deploy (customer-managed VPC) and strict audit/source-IP preservation to downstream systems. POC kickoff Tue. Need a minimal firewall/ports list, recommended topology (PrivateLink vs peering vs TGW), and a note on pricing difference if they go Dedicated/Private vs Hosted with egress. Can @Jordan or @Sam take a quick network ops call today? Customer questionnaire: https://files.example.com/finbank-q1

Mira: +1. SOC2+ and data residency in scope. They want no direct internet egress. If Private deployment, are we able to support that with our default control plane? :thinking:

Jordan: Quick thoughts — for no-internet-egress + source IP preservation I'd recommend either (1) Private deployment where workers run in their VPC, or (2) TGW + in-VPC egress proxy that preserves X-Forwarded-For. PrivateLink alone is fine for connectivity but note: if our service initiates outbound from provider side, the client IP will be SNATed unless the runtime is inside their network. Short pros/cons:
- PrivateLink: simple, good for TCP/TLS, but provider-side termination usually implies SNAT
- VPC peering: direct, low latency, but scales poorly across many accounts
- Transit Gateway: best for multi-account scale and route control

Jordan: Minimal example security group (we'll give full CIDR list in follow-up):
```
# allow outbound to Redwood control plane
sg-allow-outbound:
  - tcp 443 -> 34.197.10.0/24
  - tcp 443 -> 52.95.20.0/24
```

Sam: On the audit/source-IP ask: to preserve client IP in logs you either run model workers inside their VPC (Private deployment) or front our endpoints with an in-customer-VPC proxy that forwards X-Forwarded-For. If they require mTLS + SNI inspection, recommend terminates at their proxy and then mutual TLS to our endpoint. NAT will otherwise rewrite to our egress IPs.

SalesOps: Pricing note — Dedicated/Private has a base infra fee + per-GB egress. If traffic remains internal via PrivateLink/TGW with no internet hop we typically offer an egress credit. I'll pull specific numbers and DM the team.

Alex: They also want a concise firewall ports list for their security team and clarification on whether PrivateLink allows SNI inspection by their inline devices.

Jordan: PrivateLink behavior: if you use an NLB with TCP passthrough, SNI remains visible to their NLB/proxy. If we terminate TLS in our provider endpoint, SNI is consumed by our listener. For SNI inspection in-line you need to terminate at the customer's proxy or use TCP passthrough. For mutual TLS and client certs, Private deployment is easiest.

Mira: Can someone draft a 1-pager: recommended topology, minimal ports, and a short runbook for an on-prem proxy -> VPC path? I'll attach it to the SOC questionnaire and send to their NetSec reviewers.

Sam: I'll draft the runbook. Outline I'll cover:
- Option A: Private deployment (recommended for strict audit)
- Option B: TGW + PrivateLink endpoints (recommended for scale and multi-account)
- Option C: VPC peering (simple, fewer moving parts, limited scale)
- Sample SG/NACL rules and firewall checklist
- Quick checklist: IP allowlist, cert/mTLS steps, verification commands

NetOps Bot: New ticket created: #NET-4521 assigned to Jordan, Sam. ETA 48h.

Alex: Great. Can we sync 30m after lunch to align the runbook and pricing ask? cc @Mira :thumbsup:

Mira: 13:00 works for me.

Jordan: I can make 12:45-13:15.

Sam: 13:00 good — I'll bring the draft and sample SG snippet.

Alex: Perfect — I'll invite FinBank to the call and attach the SOC doc.
